thinking_body.plain_text_including_line_numbers:
These three values can specify a position without drawing a surface. You can read the address before seeing a sphere. This complete illustrative script is displayed here, not executed; it is not the invisible exhibit's own code.

CONCEPTS
Vector3  position  data

code.plain_text_including_line_numbers:
1 extends Node3D
 2 
 3 var point_position := Vector3(1.0, 0.5, 0.0)
 4 
 5 var marker: MeshInstance3D
 6 
 7 func _ready() -> void:
 8 	marker = MeshInstance3D.new()
 9 	var sphere := SphereMesh.new()
10 	sphere.radius = 0.04
11 	sphere.height = 0.08
12 	marker.mesh = sphere
13 	marker.position = point_position
14 	add_child(marker)
15

thinking_body.plain_text_including_line_numbers:
The complete example adds a sphere at the address. Its radius supplies a surface; its position locates the centre. Changing the radius would change what you could see without moving that centre. Geometry has begun to offer more than a location.

CONCEPTS
SphereMesh  radius  centre

11 var local_p := marker.position
12 label.text = "LOCAL (%.2f, %.2f, %.2f)" % [
